name: OPA134 / OPA2134 / OPA4134
tagline: Burr-Brown's 1997 SoundPlus FET op-amp: the classic 'laid-back Burr-Brown' first upgrade for CMoys, DACs, sound cards.

lineage.note: SoundPlus line; sheet PDS-1339C printed December 1997. OPA134 pins 1/8 are offset trim.
Kept SBOS058. Die moved to a new fab (PCN 20231219018.1, rev A→B); marking cut-over undocumented.
Authorized aftermarket; sells Burr-Brown-marked OPA2134PA stock via DigiKey Marketplace.

part_numbers.note: DIP-8. Pins 1/8 trim to SBOS058A, NC from SBOS058B; pin 5 always NC.
Green variant; possibly EOL (third-party listing only). TI E2E 772760 asks PA vs PAG4.
SOIC-8. In PCN 20231219018 list; same trim-to-NC change.
DIP-8 dual: the usual rolling part and most-faked version. Rochester sells BB stock.
SOIC-8 tube / reel (LCSC C87361). In PCN 20231219018 list. Used in Aune X1S.
DIP-14 quad, discontinued; quad now SOIC-14 only.
SOIC-14 tube and reel. In PCN 20231219018 list.

key_specs.value: 4 mA typ, 5 mA max per amplifier
2 mV max (TI page); ±0.5 mV typ old; Rev B 1.0 mV (unclear)
about 5 pA typ; Rev B gives a ± value
True FET (JFET) input; VCM (V−)+2.5 V to (V+)−3.5 V

reputation.summary: The archetypal 'laid-back Burr-Brown sound' and a common first upgrade. AudioKarma/Xonar users find it warmer than the 'clinical' LME49720; some diyAudio members prefer it to LM4562. Soomal calls it warm (偏暖) and smooth (柔润); Japanese reviewers a natural all-rounder. NwAvGuy measured OPA2134, NE5532 and LM4562 near analyzer residual. TI names OPA1656 its replacement.
typical_uses: DAC outputs: Aune X1S, Shanling H1.1, TempoTec Fantasia, Musway M1
Headphone amps: Topping NX3, Lehmann-style desktop amps
Sound cards and motherboards (G1.Sniper A88X, E-MU, Xonar)
Op-amp rolling in Fosi amps; multimedia speakers (TP30)
caveats: Measured differences are tiny; FET input adds common-mode distortion at high source impedance (Self, Groner).
Needs ±2.5 V minimum; input stops 2.5 V above V−, 3.5 V below V+. DiyEden reports low-supply instability.
TI parts from 2024–2025 may be the new die: OPA134 pins 1/8 NC, lower headroom, new ESD.
The '±18 V, 5 V/µs' complaints concern TI's NE5532 change, not OPAx134.
Results depend on the circuit; counterfeits are widespread, especially DIP-8 OPA2134PA.

counterfeit_notes: Fakes widespread, especially DIP-8 OPA2134PA (TI E2E 1321243, 534233; PedalPCB; diyAudio 377960; kokoro-navi 2011), often relabelled TL072s. Check ~4–5 mA/amp, noise, offset, marking, lot codes. Buy authorized or Rochester. New-die genuine parts may differ.

silicon_changes.summary: TI moved the die to a new fab (exit from 150 mm), same part numbers. New die: no external trim, new ESD structures, revised specs (SBOS058B; PCN 20240902002.1, 3 Sep 2024). New die confirmed on 2025 date codes. Hackaday, diyAudio and Gearspace criticise TI's 'no impact' wording.
silicon_changes.identification: No marking change; die rev A→B internal. SBOS058B = new die. Test offset and pin impedance; stock is mixed. BB-logo parts very likely old die.

spec_deltas.after: NC (do not connect); internally laser-trimmed. TI E2E says leaving an old trim network in place is harmless, while the datasheet warns not to connect.
1.0 mV per a third-party reading of SBOS058B (typ vs max unclear); TI product-page parametric still shows 2 mV max. Low confidence.

spec_deltas.before: Die rev A, legacy 150 mm fab

spec_deltas.after: Updated ESD structures; different measured pin impedances (2025 date code)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Small on paper: ~2.3 dB less headroom, 128 dB separation. No old-vs-new listening or THD comparison; hobbyists report no sonic change.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: pin-compatible, but trim circuits stop working, headroom drops, new ESD failed one customer's ICT.
silicon_changes.verification: TI E2E 1429728 confirms both PCNs and no trim; 23.6 dBu confirmed; new-die numbers from EEVblog transcript only.

revision_history.changes: Combined OPA134/2134/4134 'SoundPlus' sheet; OPA134 pins 1/8 trim. No PDS-1339A, PDS-1339B or PDS-1339D found.
TI re-issue after the acquisition; content presumed same as BB sheet.
TI format: ESD table, application, layout, support sections. Trim pins kept; headroom 23.6 dBu, separation 135 dB.
Fab transfer notice with qualification data; lists OPA134UA/2134UA/4134UA, die rev A→B. PDIP inclusion unconfirmed.
New title; OPA134 pins 1/8 NC; headroom 21.3 dBu, separation 128 dB; Ib given ±; some 600 Ω specs removed.
Datasheet change for all OPAx134 to 'accurately reflect device characteristics'; trim pins do-not-connect.
Rev B apparently re-dated 'Revised November 2024' without a new letter. No SBOS058C found.

revision_chains.note: PDS-1339C confirmed on CERN and Octopart 7265401, 33018557, 8191592. No separate dual or quad sheet.
No header-verified copy of the 2000 issue. Do the Aug and Nov 2024 Rev B files differ?

open_questions: Confirm 21.3 dBu and 135/128 dB against the PDFs; compare the full SBOS058A vs B tables.
Does PCN 20231219018 include the PDIP (PA) variants? What is the old/new die date-code cut-over?
Is SBOS058B Vos 1.0 mV typ or max? Ignore '6.5 nV/√Hz, 3.5 mV' text (another part, probably OPA2141).
How does MPN SN412008DRE4 (E2E 1626121) relate to OPA2134? Confirm OPA134PAG4 and OPA2134PAG4 status.
Which revision does each mirror hold? Check inferred sbos058a, opa4134 and focus.ti.com URLs.

refuted_claims: No SBOS058C exists; current is SBOS058B revised November 2024. Inferred sbos058c URL dropped.
SBOS058A is titled 'OPAx134 SoundPlus High Performance…'; 'High-Performance, SoundPlus' wording is Rev B.
'6.5 nV/√Hz, 2 pA, 3.5 mV max' is not an OPAx134 spec; it belongs to a 10 MHz JFET dual.
PCN 20240902002.1 is dated 3 September 2024, not 2 September.
BB PDS number found: PDS-1339C, printed December 1997.
corrections: Added https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/sbos058b/sbos058b.pdf; symlink/opa134.pdf raised to high confidence.
TI original dated September 2000; Rev A change list added.
Rev B first issued about Aug 2024, current PDF Nov 2024; Mouser.lt copy raised to medium.
Mouser 3378997 copy identified as probably SBOS058A.
PCN 20231219018.1: Mouser copy 22 Dec 2023; UA parts, die rev A→B; general notice.
PCN 20240902002.1: 3 Sep 2024, datasheet-only but changes electrical specs.
OPA4134PA obsolete; added OPA4134UA/2K5, E4 variants, OPA2134PAG4; OPA134PAG4 possibly EOL.
Confirmed 8 MHz, 20 V/µs, 4 mA/ch, 2 mV max; headroom unit is dBu (23.6 old).
Added CERN, Octopart, kyohritsu, protricom, megastar, eltim, kontest, audiodesignguide, alldatasheet and radiolocman mirrors.
